newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian 1997 global share offers seen at $10 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian 1997 global share offers seen at $10 bln.

text.p: Global share offerings by Brazilian companies were likely to reach $10 billion in 1997, compared with $500 million last year, the vice president of the country's National Development Bank (BNDES) said on Thursday.
"Brazil will place shares worth an estimated $10 billion in the markets this year," Jose Pio Borges said.
About 25 percent of those shares, offered by private companies and state-owned enterprises being privatized, are expected to be placed in the domestic market, he said.
Future privatizations of state-owned companies, starting with the sell-off of Comphania Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), would involve larger global share offers than in the past, the official said.
"Increasingly we will see large public offers," Borges said. "We will follow the CVRD model of a strategic block and a substantial global offer."

Under the CVRD sell-off rules, a global share offer of 26 to 31 percent of the company's voting shares, worth about $1.8 billion, will follow the auction of a strategic 45 percent block of voting shares and an offer to CVRD employees.
((--Simon de logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
